newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank head vows tight credit - paper.
newsitem.headline: China central bank head vows tight credit - paper.

text.p: China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong has said China will continue a relatively tight monetary policy despite falling inflation, the Hong Kong Economic Times said on Tuesday.

The People's Bank of China, the central bank, would wait for further signs that once-rampant inflation had been brought under control before relaxing its "appropriately" tight credit policy, the newspaper quoted Dai as saying.

"The central bank is not looking at the short-term performance of its interest rate policy to combat inflation, but must observe inflation stability over a relatively long period before drawing conclusions," it quoted Dai as saying.
Dai forecast China's retail price index would grow by five to six percent in 1997.
Retail price inflation, the benchmark figure China uses for nationwide inflation, was a year-on-year 2.9 percent in February, official figures show.
Retail price inflation was 6.1 percent in 1996, down from 14.8 percent in 1995 and from a communist-era high of 21.7 percent in 1994.

Dai declined to comment on speculation that he would be appointed mayor of China's financial centre of Shanghai when the ruling Communist Party reshuffles its top leadership at a party congress this October, the newspaper said.
